result.name: Lam Research Corporation
markets: Plasma etch equipment (conductor and dielectric etch)
Thin-film deposition equipment (CVD, ALD, ECD/electroplating, PVD)
Installed-base services, spares and upgrades (Customer Support Business Group)

mission.plain: Lam says it seeks to innovate at the atomic scale, building the machines that let chipmakers make ever smaller, more powerful chips.

about.plain: Lam Research builds giant, very precise machines that chip factories use to make computer chips. Its machines carve tiny patterns into silicon wafers (etching) and lay down ultra-thin layers of material (deposition), some only a few atoms thick. Chipmakers buy hundreds of these machines for each factory, and Lam then earns money keeping them running, selling spare parts and upgrading them.
about.customers: The world's biggest chipmakers, such as TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, which Lam names as its most significant customers.
about.everyday: Almost every phone, laptop and AI data-center chip, especially memory chips that store your photos and run AI, was made using Lam machines.

money.plain: Etch, deposition and clean tools for new factories; 63.2% of revenue in the June 2026 quarter

money.part: Service, spare parts and upgrades (Customer Support Business Group)
money.plain: Keeping its huge installed base of tools running and upgrading them; 36.8% of revenue in the June 2026 quarter
Machines for stacking chips (high-bandwidth memory, chiplets), including new panel-level tools; expected to grow more than 70% in 2026

money.part: Gate-all-around and backside-power etch/deposition (e.g. Akara, ALTUS Halo)
money.plain: New tools for the most advanced 2nm-and-below transistors and molybdenum wiring

result.summary: Lam has a strong competitive advantage: it is the leading supplier of plasma etch and a leader in deposition for memory chips, where its tools are qualified 'tool of record' inside customers' production lines and very costly to replace. Decades of process know-how, a huge installed base that feeds a high-margin service business, and heavy R&D ($2.38 billion in FY2026) make it hard for rivals to dislodge, although Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron are capable competitors and China's local suppliers are rising.

pricingPower.evidence: Gross margin rose from 44.6% in FY2023 to 50.5% in FY2026 while revenue grew 26% to $23.23 billion, and the company guided 52% gross margin for the September 2026 quarter on $8.1 billion revenue, showing it can lift prices and mix even as volumes surge.

moats.evidence: Among chipmakers Lam is a top-five equipment brand (ranked behind ASML and Applied Materials by TechInsights for 2025) with a large patent portfolio, but it is unknown to consumers.

Once a Lam etch or deposition tool is qualified as tool of record for a process step, changing suppliers means requalifying the process and risking yield, so customers typically keep the incumbent for the life of the node and beyond.
There is no classic network effect, though co-development with the leading memory and logic makers improves Lam's tools for all customers.

With $23.23 billion of FY2026 revenue and $2.38 billion of R&D, Lam outspends all etch/deposition rivals except Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron, and its installed base feeds a service business that produced nearly $2.5 billion in the June 2026 quarter alone.

Only a handful of firms (Lam, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron, plus niche players) can supply leading-edge etch and deposition, a market too specialised for many new entrants outside state-backed Chinese suppliers.
Lam competes head-on with incumbents using the same business model.

High-aspect-ratio etch for 200+ layer 3D NAND, conductor etch for gate-all-around (Akara) and atomic-layer processes rely on decades of accumulated plasma know-how that rivals have struggled to match.
About 23,300 employees, over 26% in R&D, but no exclusive asset; talent is contested by Applied Materials, TEL and chipmakers.

customers.evidence: Micron, Samsung, SK hynix and TSMC have been its most significant customers in each of FY2024-FY2026, and customer support revenue hit a third straight record of nearly $2.5 billion in the June 2026 quarter, up 43% year over year, showing customers keep buying upgrades and services.

talent.evidence: Lam appears on Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies list (industry rank 4 in semiconductors) and employs about 23,300 people with over 26% in R&D, but it does not feature prominently in major best-place-to-work rankings.

product.evidence: Lam is the leader in NAND high-aspect-ratio etch and a key supplier for DRAM and gate-all-around logic, with its Akara conductor etch platform winning several tool-of-record positions and its installed base doubling annually since launch, per the July 2026 earnings call.

competitors.name: Applied Materials, Inc.
competitors.note: Primary competitor in dielectric and metal deposition and in etch.

competitors.name: Tokyo Electron Limited
competitors.note: Major rival in etch (especially dielectric etch), deposition and wet clean.

competitors.name: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation (Hitachi, Ltd.)
competitors.note: Conductor etch competitor; Hitachi High-Tech is a Hitachi subsidiary.

competitors.name: ASM International N.V.
competitors.note: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and epitaxy, and PECVD.

competitors.name: NAURA Technology Group
competitors.note: Chinese supplier of etch, deposition and clean tools gaining share in China.

competitors.name: Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment Inc. (AMEC)
competitors.note: Chinese etch and MOCVD supplier competing in China's fabs.

competitors.name: Wonik IPS
competitors.note: Korean ALD and PECVD supplier, mainly to Samsung.

competitors.name: SEMES Co., Ltd.
competitors.note: Samsung-owned supplier of cleaning and other equipment.

competitors.name: Kokusai Electric Corporation
competitors.note: Batch deposition and ALD furnaces, especially for 3D NAND.

competitors.name: KLA Corporation
competitors.note: Mainly process control; competes for the same fab budgets rather than directly in etch/deposition.

threats: US export controls on China, which was 26% of revenue in the June 2026 quarter, and could tighten further
Chinese state-backed rivals (NAURA, AMEC, Piotech) taking share in China's mature-node fabs
Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron winning tool-of-record positions at new nodes (gate-all-around, backside power, 3D DRAM)
Deep cyclicality of memory capex: revenue fell 14.5% in FY2024 after the memory downturn
Customer concentration in a few chipmakers (TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, Micron) and a slowdown in AI data-center spending
Shift of process steps toward lithography or new integration schemes that reduce etch/deposition intensity

ceo.name: Timothy M. Archer
ceo.background: B.S. in applied physics from Caltech, Harvard Program for Management Development; 18 years at Novellus Systems (COO), joined Lam in 2012 as COO

c1.evidence: Lam leads etch and is a deposition leader in a semiconductor equipment industry that grew to about $136 billion in 2025 (TechInsights) and is expanding with AI, but the industry is mature and cyclical rather than newly emerging.

c2.evidence: Chipmakers choose Lam for unmatched high-aspect-ratio etch and atomic-scale deposition know-how, and once qualified as tool of record the tools are rarely replaced, an advantage built over decades that is hard to copy.

c3.evidence: Lam is a default leader for chipmakers in etch, but ordinary people do not recognise the name.

c4.evidence: Lam talks about innovating 'at the atomic scale' to enable chip progress, but it publishes no prominent mission statement and management messaging centres on financial targets like its 2028 model.

c6.evidence: “chip equipment, etch, cyclical” – among investors and engineers the impression is mostly positive (a high-quality AI and memory beneficiary), while the general public barely knows it.

c7.evidence: Lam raised its 2026 wafer-fab-equipment outlook to the low-$150 billion range in July 2026, driven by AI, high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

c8.evidence: Lam is expanding into advanced packaging (expected to grow over 70% in 2026, with panel-level tools), gate-all-around, backside power and molybdenum metallisation, but all remain within chip-making equipment.

m1.evidence: Archer has articulated a clear view that AI drives more etch and deposition intensity (e.g. served market per NAND wafer doubling from 128 to 500+ layers), though he is an operator more than a public visionary.

m2.evidence: Archer is not a founder but a 30+ year industry veteran (Novellus then Lam since 2012) who invests through cycles, e.g. growing R&D to $2.38 billion in FY2026.

m4.evidence: There is little public evidence either way about a servant-leadership style at Lam.

m5.evidence: Under Archer Lam has kept launching new platforms (Akara, Kiyo, ALTUS Halo, Striker, panel packaging tools), but its culture is not widely described as distinctive.

m6.evidence: Archer holds a B.S. in applied physics from Caltech and began his career as an engineer at Tektronix in 1989 before running process technology at Novellus.

m7.evidence: No controversies are known, but there is little public record showing a cause beyond running the business well.

m7b.evidence: No commencement speech by Tim Archer at a top university could be found.

m8b.evidence: Archer has a low-key, engineering-focused public persona.

m9.evidence: Since Archer became CEO in December 2018 revenue rose from $14.63 billion in FY2021 to $23.23 billion in FY2026 and operating margin reached 35.3%, a company record.

m10.evidence: Lam is not known for notable frugality, though its operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue in FY2026.

c10.evidence: Its tools are behind almost every memory and logic chip in phones, PCs and AI servers worldwide, but the benefit is indirect.

p2.evidence: Etching holes 100+ times deeper than they are wide across 200+ layer 3D NAND, or depositing films a few atoms thick, is among the hardest manufacturing tasks in the world and essential to all modern chips.

f1.evidence: Revenue grew in FY2022, FY2025 and FY2026 and was flat-up in FY2023 ($17.43 billion), but fell 14.5% to $14.91 billion in FY2024.

f2.evidence: Gross margin rose from 46.5% in FY2021 to 50.5% in FY2026 and operating margin from 30.6% to 35.3%, though both dipped in FY2023-FY2024.

f3.evidence: At June 28, 2026 cash was $5.58 billion against $3.73 billion of debt and finance leases, with $5.86 billion operating cash flow in FY2026 and equity of $12.47 billion.

f4.evidence: Operating income rose from $4.48 billion in FY2021 to $8.20 billion in FY2026 and operating cash flow from $3.59 billion to $5.86 billion, but both dipped in FY2024 and cash flow fell from $6.17 billion in FY2025.

v1.evidence: Lam is widely seen as the best in high-aspect-ratio etch for memory, but Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron lead in other steps, so it is not clearly best across every alternative.

v2.evidence: Lam is on Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies list (4th in semiconductors) but not on major best-employer lists such as Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For.

c5.evidence: If Lam vanished, memory makers like Samsung, SK hynix and Micron and foundries like TSMC would struggle to produce chips, disrupting phones, PCs and AI data centers worldwide.
